ESV.1: When Samuel became old, he made his sons judges over Israel.
ESV.2: The name of his firstborn son was Joel, and the name of his second, Abijah; they were judges in Beersheba.
ESV.3: Yet his sons did not walk in his ways but turned aside after gain. They took bribes and perverted justice.
ESV.4: Then all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah
ESV.5: and said to him, “Behold, you are old and your sons do not walk in your ways. Now appoint for us a king to judge us like all the nations.”
ESV.6: But the thing displeased Samuel when they said, “Give us a king to judge us.” And Samuel prayed to the LORD.
ESV.7: And the LORD said to Samuel, “Obey the voice of the people in all that they say to you, for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected me from being king over them.
ESV.8: According to all the deeds that they have done, from the day I brought them up out of Egypt even to this day, forsaking me and serving other gods, so they are also doing to you.
ESV.9: Now then, obey their voice; only you shall solemnly warn them and show them the ways of the king who shall reign over them.”
ESV.10: So Samuel told all the words of the LORD to the people who were asking for a king from him.
ESV.11: He said, “These will be the ways of the king who will reign over you: he will take your sons and appoint them to his chariots and to be his horsemen and to run before his chariots.
ESV.12: And he will appoint for himself commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties, and some to plow his ground and to reap his harvest, and to make his implements of war and the equipment of his chariots.
ESV.13: He will take your daughters to be perfumers and cooks and bakers.
ESV.14: He will take the best of your fields and vineyards and olive orchards and give them to his servants.
ESV.15: He will take the tenth of your grain and of your vineyards and give it to his officers and to his servants.
ESV.16: He will take your male servants and female servants and the best of your young men  and your donkeys, and put them to his work.
ESV.17: He will take the tenth of your flocks, and you shall be his slaves.
ESV.18: And in that day you will cry out because of your king, whom you have chosen for yourselves, but the LORD will not answer you in that day.”
ESV.19: But the people refused to obey the voice of Samuel. And they said, “No! But there shall be a king over us,
ESV.20: that we also may be like all the nations, and that our king may judge us and go out before us and fight our battles.”
ESV.21: And when Samuel had heard all the words of the people, he repeated them in the ears of the LORD.
ESV.22: And the LORD said to Samuel, “Obey their voice and make them a king.” Samuel then said to the men of Israel, “Go every man to his city.”

NKJV.1: Now it came to pass when Samuel was old that he made his sons judges over Israel.
NKJV.2: The name of his firstborn was Joel, and the name of his second, Abijah; they were judges in Beersheba.
NKJV.3: But his sons did not walk in his ways; they turned aside after dishonest gain, took bribes, and perverted justice.
NKJV.4: Then all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah,
NKJV.5: and said to him, “Look, you are old, and your sons do not walk in your ways. Now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.”
NKJV.6: But the thing displeased Samuel when they said, “Give us a king to judge us.” So Samuel prayed to the LORD.
NKJV.7: And the LORD said to Samuel, “Heed the voice of the people in all that they say to you; for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected Me, that I should not reign over them.
NKJV.8: According to all the works which they have done since the day that I brought them up out of Egypt, even to this day—with which they have forsaken Me and served other gods—so they are doing to you also.
NKJV.9: Now therefore, heed their voice. However, you shall solemnly forewarn them, and show them the behavior of the king who will reign over them.”
NKJV.10: So Samuel told all the words of the LORD to the people who asked him for a king.
NKJV.11: And he said, “This will be the behavior of the king who will reign over you: He will take your sons and appoint them for his own chariots and to be his horsemen, and some will run before his chariots.
NKJV.12: He will appoint captains over his thousands and captains over his fifties, will set some to plow his ground and reap his harvest, and some to make his weapons of war and equipment for his chariots.
NKJV.13: He will take your daughters to be perfumers, cooks, and bakers.
NKJV.14: And he will take the best of your fields, your vineyards, and your olive groves, and give them to his servants.
NKJV.15: He will take a tenth of your grain and your vintage, and give it to his officers and servants.
NKJV.16: And he will take your male servants, your female servants, your finest young men, and your donkeys, and put them to his work.
NKJV.17: He will take a tenth of your sheep. And you will be his servants.
NKJV.18: And you will cry out in that day because of your king whom you have chosen for yourselves, and the LORD will not hear you in that day.”
NKJV.19: Nevertheless the people refused to obey the voice of Samuel; and they said, “No, but we will have a king over us,
NKJV.20: that we also may be like all the nations, and that our king may judge us and go out before us and fight our battles.”
NKJV.21: And Samuel heard all the words of the people, and he repeated them in the hearing of the LORD.
NKJV.22: So the LORD said to Samuel, “Heed their voice, and make them a king.” And Samuel said to the men of Israel, “Every man go to his city.”

NASB.1: And it came about when Samuel was old that he appointed his sons judges over Israel.
NASB.2: Now the name of his firstborn was Joel, and the name of his second, Abijah; [they] were judging in Beersheba.
NASB.3: His sons, however, did not walk in his ways, but turned aside after dishonest gain and took bribes and perverted justice.
NASB.4: Then all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah;
NASB.5: and they said to him, 'Behold, you have grown old, and your sons do not walk in your ways. Now appoint a king for us to judge us like all the nations.'
NASB.6: But the thing was displeasing in the sight of Samuel when they said, 'Give us a king to judge us.' And Samuel prayed to the LORD.
NASB.7: The LORD said to Samuel, 'Listen to the voice of the people in regard to all that they say to you, for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected Me from being king over them.
NASB.8: 'Like all the deeds which they have done since the day that I brought them up from Egypt even to this day-- in that they have forsaken Me and served other gods-- so they are doing to you also.
NASB.9: 'Now then, listen to their voice; however, you shall solemnly warn them and tell them of the procedure of the king who will reign over them.'
NASB.10: So Samuel spoke all the words of the LORD to the people who had asked of him a king.
NASB.11: He said, 'This will be the procedure of the king who will reign over you: he will take your sons and place [them] for himself in his chariots and among his horsemen and they will run before his chariots.
NASB.12: 'He will appoint for himself commanders of thousands and of fifties, and [some] to do his plowing and to reap his harvest and to make his weapons of war and equipment for his chariots.
NASB.13: 'He will also take your daughters for perfumers and cooks and bakers.
NASB.14: 'He will take the best of your fields and your vineyards and your olive groves and give [them] to his servants.
NASB.15: 'He will take a tenth of your seed and of your vineyards and give to his officers and to his servants.
NASB.16: 'He will also take your male servants and your female servants and your best young men and your donkeys and use [them] for his work.
NASB.17: 'He will take a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves will become his servants.
NASB.18: 'Then you will cry out in that day because of your king whom you have chosen for yourselves, but the LORD will not answer you in that day.'
NASB.19: Nevertheless, the people refused to listen to the voice of Samuel, and they said, 'No, but there shall be a king over us,
NASB.20: that we also may be like all the nations, that our king may judge us and go out before us and fight our battles.'
NASB.21: Now after Samuel had heard all the words of the people, he repeated them in the LORD'S hearing.
NASB.22: The LORD said to Samuel, 'Listen to their voice and appoint them a king.' So Samuel said to the men of Israel, 'Go every man to his city.'

WEB.1: When Samuel was old, he made his sons judges over Israel.
WEB.2: Now the name of his firstborn was Joel; and the name of his second, Abijah. They were judges in Beersheba.
WEB.3: His sons didn’t walk in his ways, but turned aside after dishonest gain, took bribes, and perverted justice.
WEB.4: Then all the elders of Israel gathered themselves together and came to Samuel to Ramah.
WEB.5: They said to him, “Behold, you are old, and your sons don’t walk in your ways. Now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.”
WEB.6: But the thing displeased Samuel, when they said, “Give us a king to judge us.” Samuel prayed to Yahweh.
WEB.7: Yahweh said to Samuel, “Listen to the voice of the people in all that they tell you; for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected me as the king over them.
WEB.8: According to all the works which they have done since the day that I brought them up out of Egypt even to this day, in that they have forsaken me, and served other gods, so they also do to you.
WEB.9: Now therefore listen to their voice. However you shall protest solemnly to them, and shall show them the way of the king who will reign over them.”
WEB.10: Samuel told all Yahweh’s words to the people who asked him for a king.
WEB.11: He said, “This will be the way of the king who shall reign over you: he will take your sons, and appoint them as his servants, for his chariots, and to be his horsemen; and they will run before his chariots.
WEB.12: He will appoint them to him for captains of thousands, and captains of fifties; and he will assign some to plow his ground, and to reap his harvest, and to make his instruments of war, and the instruments of his chariots.
WEB.13: He will take your daughters to be perfumers, to be cooks, and to be bakers.
WEB.14: He will take your fields, your vineyards, and your olive groves, even their best, and give them to his servants.
WEB.15: He will take one tenth of your seed, and of your vineyards, and give it to his officers, and to his servants.
WEB.16: He will take your male servants, your female servants, your best young men, and your donkeys, and assign them to his own work.
WEB.17: He will take one tenth of your flocks; and you will be his servants.
WEB.18: You will cry out in that day because of your king whom you will have chosen for yourselves; and Yahweh will not answer you in that day.”
WEB.19: But the people refused to listen to the voice of Samuel; and they said, “No; but we will have a king over us,
WEB.20: that we also may be like all the nations, and that our king may judge us, and go out before us, and fight our battles.”
WEB.21: Samuel heard all the words of the people, and he rehearsed them in the ears of Yahweh.
WEB.22: Yahweh said to Samuel, “Listen to their voice, and make them a king.” Samuel said to the men of Israel, “Everyone go to your own city.”

AMP.1: And it came about when Samuel was old that he appointed his sons as judges over Israel.
AMP.2: Now the name of his firstborn was Joel, and the name of his second, Abijah; they were judging in Beersheba.
AMP.3: His sons, however, did not walk in his ways, but turned aside after dishonest gain, took bribes, and perverted justice.
AMP.4: Then all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah
AMP.5: and said to him, "Look, you have grown old, and your sons do not walk in your ways. Now appoint us a king to judge us [and rule over us] like all the other nations."
AMP.6: But their demand displeased Samuel when they said, "Give us a king to judge and rule over us." So Samuel prayed to the LORD.
AMP.7: The LORD said to Samuel, "Listen to the voice of the people in regard to all that they say to you, for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected Me from being King over them.
AMP.8: Like all the deeds which they have done since the day that I brought them up from Egypt even to this day—in that they have abandoned (rejected) Me and served other gods—so they are doing to you also.
AMP.9: So now listen to their voice; only solemnly warn them and tell them the ways of the king who will reign over them."
AMP.10: So Samuel told all the words of the LORD to the people who were asking him for a king.
AMP.11: He said, "These will be the ways of the king who will reign over you: he will take your sons and appoint them for himself to his chariots and among his horsemen and they will run before his chariots.
AMP.12: He will appoint them for himself to be commanders over thousands and over fifties, and some to do his plowing and to reap his harvest and to make his implements of war and equipment for his chariots.
AMP.13: He will take your daughters to be perfumers, cooks, and bakers.
AMP.14: He will take the best of your fields, your vineyards, and your olive groves, and give them to his servants.
AMP.15: He will take a tenth of your grain and of your vineyards and give it to his officers and to his servants.
AMP.16: He will take your male servants and your female servants and your best young men and your donkeys and use them for his work.
AMP.17: He will take a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves shall be his servants.
AMP.18: Then you will cry out on that day because of your king whom you have chosen for yourselves, but the LORD will not answer you on that day [because you have rejected Him as King]."
AMP.19: Nevertheless, the people refused to listen to the voice of Samuel, and they said, "No, but there shall be a king over us,
AMP.20: so that we too may be like all the nations [around us], that our king may judge [and govern] us and go out before us and fight our battles."
AMP.21: Samuel had heard all the words of the people and repeated them to the LORD.
AMP.22: And the LORD said to Samuel, "Listen to their request and appoint a king for them." So Samuel said to the men of Israel, "Go, each man to his own city."

NLT.1: As Samuel grew old, he appointed his sons to be judges over Israel.
NLT.2: Joel and Abijah, his oldest sons, held court in Beersheba.
NLT.3: But they were not like their father, for they were greedy for money. They accepted bribes and perverted justice.
NLT.4: Finally, all the elders of Israel met at Ramah to discuss the matter with Samuel.
NLT.5: “Look,” they told him, “you are now old, and your sons are not like you. Give us a king to judge us like all the other nations have.”
NLT.6: Samuel was displeased with their request and went to the LORD for guidance.
NLT.7: “Do everything they say to you,” the LORD replied, “for they are rejecting me, not you. They don’t want me to be their king any longer.
NLT.8: Ever since I brought them from Egypt they have continually abandoned me and followed other gods. And now they are giving you the same treatment.
NLT.9: Do as they ask, but solemnly warn them about the way a king will reign over them.”
NLT.10: So Samuel passed on the LORD’s warning to the people who were asking him for a king.
NLT.11: “This is how a king will reign over you,” Samuel said. “The king will draft your sons and assign them to his chariots and his charioteers, making them run before his chariots.
NLT.12: Some will be generals and captains in his army, some will be forced to plow in his fields and harvest his crops, and some will make his weapons and chariot equipment.
NLT.13: The king will take your daughters from you and force them to cook and bake and make perfumes for him.
NLT.14: He will take away the best of your fields and vineyards and olive groves and give them to his own officials.
NLT.15: He will take a tenth of your grain and your grape harvest and distribute it among his officers and attendants.
NLT.16: He will take your male and female slaves and demand the finest of your cattle and donkeys for his own use.
NLT.17: He will demand a tenth of your flocks, and you will be his slaves.
NLT.18: When that day comes, you will beg for relief from this king you are demanding, but then the LORD will not help you.”
NLT.19: But the people refused to listen to Samuel’s warning. “Even so, we still want a king,” they said.
NLT.20: “We want to be like the nations around us. Our king will judge us and lead us into battle.”
NLT.21: So Samuel repeated to the LORD what the people had said,
NLT.22: and the LORD replied, “Do as they say, and give them a king.” Then Samuel agreed and sent the people home.

CSB17.1: When Samuel grew old, he appointed his sons as judges over Israel. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.2: His firstborn son’s name was Joel and his second was Abijah. They were judges in Beer-sheba. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.3: However, his sons did not walk in his ways — they turned toward dishonest profit, took bribes, and perverted justice. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.4: So all the elders of Israel gathered together and went to Samuel at Ramah. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.5: They said to him, “Look, you are old, and your sons do not walk in your ways. Therefore, appoint a king to judge us the same as all the other nations have.” <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.6: When they said, “Give us a king to judge us,” Samuel considered their demand wrong, so he prayed to the LORD.
CSB17.7: But the LORD told him, “Listen to the people and everything they say to you. They have not rejected you; they have rejected me as their king. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.8: They are doing the same thing to you that they have done to me, <sup>[1]</sup> since the day I brought them out of Egypt until this day, abandoning me and worshiping other gods.
CSB17.9: Listen to them, but solemnly warn them <sup>ⓓ</sup> and tell them about the customary rights of the king who will reign over them.”
CSB17.10: Samuel told all the LORD’s words to the people who were asking him for a king.
CSB17.11: He said, “These are the rights of the king who will reign over you: He will take your sons and put them to his use in his chariots, on his horses, or running in front of his chariots.
CSB17.12: He can appoint them for his use as commanders of thousands or commanders of fifties, <sup>ⓔ</sup> to plow his ground and reap his harvest, or to make his weapons of war and the equipment for his chariots.
CSB17.13: He can take your daughters to become perfumers, cooks, and bakers.
CSB17.14: He can take your best fields, vineyards, and olive orchards and give them to his servants. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.15: He can take a tenth of your grain and your vineyards and give them to his officials and servants.
CSB17.16: He can take your male servants, your female servants, your best young men, <sup>[2]</sup> and your donkeys and use them for his work.
CSB17.17: He can take a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves can become his servants.
CSB17.18: When that day comes, you will cry out because of the king you’ve chosen for yourselves, <sup>ⓖ</sup> but the LORD won’t answer you on that day.” <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.19: The people refused to listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We must have a king over us.
CSB17.20: Then we’ll be like all the other nations: our king will judge us, go out before us, <sup>ⓘ</sup> and fight our battles.”
CSB17.21: Samuel listened to all the people’s words and then repeated them to the LORD. <sup>[3]</sup>
CSB17.22: “Listen to them,” the LORD told Samuel. “Appoint a king for them.” <sup>ⓙ</sup> Then Samuel told the men of Israel, “Each of you, go back to your city.”

NRSVCE.8: Just as they have done to me, from the day I brought them up out of Egypt to this day, forsaking me and serving other gods, so also they are doing to you.
NRSVCE.9: Now then, listen to their voice; only — you shall solemnly warn them, and show them the ways of the king who shall reign over them.”
NRSVCE.10: So Samuel reported all the words of the LORD to the people who were asking him for a king.
NRSVCE.11: He said, “These will be the ways of the king who will reign over you: he will take your sons and appoint them to his chariots and to be his horsemen, and to run before his chariots;
NRSVCE.12: and he will appoint for himself commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties, and some to plow his ground and to reap his harvest, and to make his implements of war and the equipment of his chariots.
NRSVCE.13: He will take your daughters to be perfumers and cooks and bakers.
NRSVCE.14: He will take the best of your fields and vineyards and olive orchards and give them to his courtiers.
NRSVCE.15: He will take one-tenth of your grain and of your vineyards and give it to his officers and his courtiers.
NRSVCE.16: He will take your male and female slaves, and the best of your cattle and donkeys, and put them to his work.
NRSVCE.17: He will take one-tenth of your flocks, and you shall be his slaves.

NRSVCE.21: When Samuel had heard all the words of the people, he repeated them in the ears of the LORD.
NRSVCE.22: The LORD said to Samuel, “Listen to their voice and set a king over them.” Samuel then said to the people of Israel, “Each of you return home.”

NIV.1:
Israel Asks for a King
When Samuel grew old, he appointed his sons as judges for Israel.
NIV.2: The name of his firstborn was Joel and the name of his second was Abijah, and they served at Beersheba.
NIV.3: But his sons did not walk in his ways. They turned aside after dishonest gain and accepted bribes and perverted justice.
NIV.4: So all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah.
NIV.5: They said to him, “You are old, and your sons do not walk in your ways; now appoint a king to lead us, such as all the other nations have.”
NIV.6: But when they said, “Give us a king to lead us,” this displeased Samuel; so he prayed to the Lord.
NIV.7: And the Lord told him: “Listen to all that the people are saying to you; it is not you they have rejected, but they have rejected me as their king.
NIV.8: As they have done from the day I brought them up out of Egypt until this day, forsaking me and serving other gods, so they are doing to you.
NIV.9: Now listen to them; but warn them solemnly and let them know what the king who will reign over them will do.”
NIV.10: Samuel told all the words of the Lord to the people who were asking him for a king.
NIV.11: He said, “This is what the king who will reign over you will do: He will take your sons and make them serve with his chariots and horses, and they will run in front of his chariots.
NIV.12: Some he will assign to be commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties, and others to plow his ground and reap his harvest, and still others to make weapons of war and equipment for his chariots.
NIV.13: He will take your daughters to be perfumers and cooks and bakers.
NIV.14: He will take the best of your fields and vineyards and olive groves and give them to his attendants.
NIV.15: He will take a tenth of your grain and of your vintage and give it to his officials and attendants.
NIV.16: Your menservants and maidservants and the best of your cattle and donkeys he will take for his own use.
NIV.17: He will take a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves will become his slaves.
NIV.18: When that day comes, you will cry out for relief from the king you have chosen, and the Lord will not answer you in that day.”
NIV.19: But the people refused to listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We want a king over us.
NIV.20: Then we will be like all the other nations, with a king to lead us and to go out before us and fight our battles.”
NIV.21: When Samuel heard all that the people said, he repeated it before the Lord.
NIV.22:
The Lord answered, “Listen to them and give them a king.”
Then Samuel said to the men of Israel, “Everyone go back to his town.”

NET.1: In his old age Samuel appointed his sons as judges over Israel.
NET.2: The name of his firstborn son was Joel, and the name of his second son was Abijah. They were judges in Beer Sheba.
NET.3: But his sons did not follow his ways. Instead, they made money dishonestly, accepted bribes, and perverted justice.
NET.4: So all the elders of Israel gathered together and approached Samuel at Ramah.
NET.5: They said to him, “Look, you are old, and your sons don’t follow your ways. So now appoint over us a king to lead us, just like all the other nations have.”
NET.6: But this request displeased Samuel, for they said, “Give us a king to lead us.” So Samuel prayed to the LORD.
NET.7: The LORD said to Samuel, “Do everything the people request of you. For it is not you that they have rejected, but it is me that they have rejected as their king.
NET.8: Just as they have done from the day that I brought them up from Egypt until this very day, they have rejected me and have served other gods. This is what they are also doing to you.
NET.9: So now do as they say. But seriously warn them and make them aware of the policies of the king who will rule over them.”
NET.10: So Samuel spoke all the words of the LORD to the people who were asking him for a king.
NET.11: He said, “Here are the policies of the king who will rule over you: He will conscript your sons and put them in his chariot forces and in his cavalry; they will run in front of his chariot.
NET.12: He will appoint for himself leaders of thousands and leaders of fifties, as well as those who plow his ground, reap his harvest, and make his weapons of war and his chariot equipment.
NET.13: He will take your daughters to be ointment makers, cooks, and bakers.
NET.14: He will take your best fields and vineyards and give them to his own servants.
NET.15: He will demand a tenth of your seed and of the produce of your vineyards and give it to his administrators and his servants.
NET.16: He will take your male and female servants, as well as your best cattle and your donkeys, and assign them for his own use.
NET.17: He will demand a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves will be his servants.
NET.18: In that day you will cry out because of your king whom you have chosen for yourselves, but the LORD won’t answer you in that day.”
NET.19: But the people refused to heed Samuel’s warning. Instead they said, “No! There will be a king over us!
NET.20: We will be like all the other nations. Our king will judge us and lead us and fight our battles.”
NET.21: So Samuel listened to everything the people said and then reported it to the LORD.
NET.22: The LORD said to Samuel, “Do as they say and install a king over them.” Then Samuel said to the men of Israel, “Each of you go back to his own city.”

MSG.1: When Samuel got to be an old man, he set his sons up as judges in Israel.
MSG.2: His firstborn son was named Joel, the name of his second, Abijah. They were assigned duty in Beersheba.
MSG.3: But his sons didn't take after him; they were out for what they could get for themselves, taking bribes, corrupting justice.
MSG.4: Fed up, all the elders of Israel got together and confronted Samuel at Ramah.
MSG.5: They presented their case: "Look, you're an old man, and your sons aren't following in your footsteps. Here's what we want you to do: Appoint a king to rule us, just like everybody else."
MSG.6: When Samuel heard their demand—"Give us a king to rule us!"—he was crushed. How awful! Samuel prayed to God.
MSG.7: God answered Samuel, "Go ahead and do what they're asking. They are not rejecting you. They've rejected me as their King.
MSG.8: From the day I brought them out of Egypt until this very day they've been behaving like this, leaving me for other gods. And now they're doing it to you.
MSG.9: So let them have their own way. But warn them of what they're in for. Tell them the way kings operate, just what they're likely to get from a king."
MSG.10: So Samuel told them, delivered God's warning to the people who were asking him to give them a king.
MSG.11: He said, "This is the way the kind of king you're talking about operates. He'll take your sons and make soldiers of them—chariotry, cavalry, infantry,
MSG.12: regimented in battalions and squadrons. He'll put some to forced labor on his farms, plowing and harvesting, and others to making either weapons of war or chariots in which he can ride in luxury.
MSG.13: He'll put your daughters to work as beauticians and waitresses and cooks.
MSG.14: He'll conscript your best fields, vineyards, and orchards and hand them over to his special friends.
MSG.15: He'll tax your harvests and vintage to support his extensive bureaucracy.
MSG.16: Your prize workers and best animals he'll take for his own use.
MSG.17: He'll lay a tax on your flocks and you'll end up no better than slaves.
MSG.18: The day will come when you will cry in desperation because of this king you so much want for yourselves. But don't expect God to answer."
MSG.19: But the people wouldn't listen to Samuel. "No!" they said. "We will have a king to rule us!
MSG.20: Then we'll be just like all the other nations. Our king will rule us and lead us and fight our battles."
MSG.21: Samuel took in what they said and rehearsed it with God.
MSG.22:
God told Samuel, "Do what they say. Make them a king."
Then Samuel dismissed the men of Israel: "Go home, each of you to your own city."
